findings.title: Large response construction and encoding block the event loop
findings.description: After the database read returns, the async handler synchronously builds the response model and calls `timeseries_response`, which performs `model_dump` and JSON or msgpack encoding on the event-loop thread. The row ceiling permits 75,000 candles; the project’s load-test documentation records a response of about 34.8 MB at that size. This CPU work can delay unrelated requests while it runs. Keep the connection released before serialization, but move model construction and encoding off the event loop (and cover the concurrent large-response path in a load test). The trades route has the same issue at lines 173-174.

findings.title: Trade completeness field description misstates the watermark
findings.description: The OpenAPI description says `tape_complete_through` is the “Created time of the newest stored trade.” The route populates it from `sync_state['trades'].watermark_ts`, which represents the end of the last fully walked window—not the newest stored trade. This distinction matters when interpreting an empty time window; describe it as the tape’s completeness watermark instead.
